course_name_original: Ciencia e Ingeniería de los Materiales

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the fundamentals of materials science, technology, and chemistry. Understand the relationship between microstructure, synthesis or processing, and material properties.
Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to apply knowledge in practice.
Aptitude for oral and written communication in the native language.
Ability to use computers fluently at a user level.
Competence in the sustainable use of resources and in the prevention of negative impacts on the natural and social environment.
Be able to apply the fundamentals of materials science, technology, and chemistry.
Be able to understand the relationship between microstructure, synthesis or processing, and properties of materials.
Know and apply the methodology for conducting materials tests. Interpret the measurements obtained in these tests.

syllabus_topics: Theoretical unit 1. Introduction to Materials Science and Engineering 1.1. Presentation 1.1.1. Syllabus. Methodology. Evaluation system. 1.2. Materials Science and Engineering. 1.2.1. Concept of material. 1.2.2. Material classification. 1.2.3. Evolution of engineering materials. 1.2.4. Advanced materials. 1.2.5. Sustainability and material recycling.

Theoretical and problem unit 2.1. Crystalline structures 2.1.1. Crystalline structures in metals. 2.1.2. Notations for crystalline positions, directions, and planes. 2.1.3. Polymorphism and allotropy. Non-crystalline materials.
Theoretical and problem unit 2.2. Crystalline imperfections 2.2.1. Point defects. 2.2.2. Dislocations. 2.2.3. Surface defects. 2.2.4. Microscopic observation.
Theoretical and problem unit 2.3. Diffusion in solids 2.3.1. Atomic mechanisms of diffusion: 2.3.2. Steady-state diffusion. 2.3.3. Non-steady-state diffusion. 2.3.4. Factors affecting diffusion.
Theoretical and problem unit 3.1. Basic mechanical properties. 3.1.1. Elastic deformation. 3.1.2. Plastic deformation. 3.1.3. Tensile test. 3.1.4. Hardness.
Theoretical and problem unit 3.2. Fracture 3.2.1. Fracture. 3.2.2. Impact tests. Ductile-brittle transition. 3.2.3. Fatigue. 3.2.4. Creep.

Theoretical and problem unit 4.1. Plastic deformation in metals 4.1.1. Dislocations and plastic deformation. 4.1.2. Strengthening mechanisms in single-phase systems. 4.1.3. Recovery. Recrystallization. Grain growth.
Theoretical and problem unit 4.2. Phase diagrams 4.2.1. Definitions and fundamental concepts. 4.2.2. Phase diagrams of binary alloy systems 4.2.3. The Fe-C system.
Theoretical and problem unit 4.3. Phase transformations 4.3.1. Kinetics of solid-state reactions. 4.3.2. Microstructural changes in Fe-C alloys. 4.3.3. Tempering.

Theoretical and problem unit for GIE and GIEI 5.1. Electrical and magnetic properties of materials 5.1.1. Electrical conduction 5.1.2. Semiconductors 5.1.3. Dielectric behavior 5.1.4. Basic concepts of magnetism 5.1.5. Diamagnetism and paramagnetism. Ferromagnetism 5.16. Soft and hard magnetic materials Theoretical and problem unit for GIM and GITI 5.1 Metallic alloys 5.1.1 Heat treatments 5.1.2 Processing 5.1.3 Alloys.

Non-contact guided reading (4h) and autonomous learning 5.2. Ceramic materials 5.2.1. Crystalline structures of simple ceramics and silicates. 5.2.2. Glasses and glass-ceramics 5.2.3. Processing of ceramic materials.

Non-contact guided reading (4h) and autonomous learning 5.3. Polymeric materials 5.3.1. Polymer structures. 5.3.2. Mechanical and thermomechanical characteristics. 5.3.3. Applications and shaping of polymers.

Non-contact guided reading (4h) and autonomous learning 5.4. Composite materials 5.4.1. Particle-reinforced composite materials 5.4.2. Fiber-reinforced composite materials. 5.4.3. Structural composite materials.
Practical unit in the workshop-laboratory Heat treatments: Normalizing, quenching, tempering of F-114 steel Charpy tests: impact toughness.
Practical unit Hardness tests of steel specimens with different heat treatments using Rockwell, Vickers, and Brinell techniques.
Practical unit Influence of steel heat treatments on their mechanical behavior using the tensile test.
Practical unit Determination of defects and cracks by non-destructive testing.

assessment_methods.method: Completion of questionnaires on topics taught in face-to-face classes
Completion of 3 tests on guided readings to evaluate autonomous learning
Completion of 5 practical sessions and technical reports, including follow-up activities
Final exam on topics taught in lectures

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on questionnaires (10%), 3 guided reading tests (9%), practical sessions and technical reports (11%), and a final exam (70%). A minimum score of 4 out of 10 is required on the final exam.
